findings.summary: The current candidate has no mechanism implementing the unchanged coverage/failure promise; its stale permission is unbounded.
findings.evidence: 63/intent.md What we want 1/4 and spec.md:30-33,45-52 require coverage and no admission while controller/metadata is absent. design.md:76-98 identifies this gap but supplies neither a revocable permission nor the proposed bounded alternative's bound. After an eligible permit PDB is set to minAvailable=0, stopping the controller leaves it permissive indefinitely; the slot PDB still permits one disruption. Separately, Kubernetes v1.36.5 eviction.go:358-363 skips every PDB for Pending, terminal or already-deleting pods, so initial/replacement markers are an actual ordinary-eviction coverage gap, not merely a fake-client uncertainty. Pinned primary source: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go#L356-L363 . A Lease and 5s reconciliation supply no expiry at the eviction linearization point. This is a missing technical contract, not a missing human approval.
findings.fix: Keep this defect unresolved and transfer the unchanged original guard slice, all drafts and this finding to the authorized dedicated owner. Preserve the user's instruction that #63 does not select either option. The owner's ADR/owning plan must resolve (a) an explicitly changed best-effort contract with a concrete enforceable finite failure window and exact uncovered states/bypasses, or (b) exact synchronous fail-closed admission/enrollment rules and atomic admission ordering. Specify node appearance, pending/terminal/replacement markers, controller death after grant, metadata loss and leader overlap, with pinned real-API fixtures that demonstrate the selected contract. #63 may become the composition/acceptance wrapper and wait for the owner's actual clear review; an unspecified future gate cannot clear the current mechanism.

findings.summary: Required node affinity cannot bind a marker to immutable Node UID under the proposed node-read-only contract.
findings.evidence: design.md:47-49 requires required node affinity to the exact Node identity; :69-74 and spec.md:64-66 promise recreation cannot inherit a grant, while design.md:110-116 forbids node writes. Pinned Kubernetes v1.36.5 core validation accepts only metadata.name in node-affinity matchFields (validation.go:4610-4633), not metadata.uid: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4610-L4633 . A UID in a Deployment name/ownerReference does not constrain scheduler placement. Binding by node name/hostname allows an old Deployment to place another old-grant marker on a newly created same-name Node before asynchronous garbage collection/reconciliation; selecting a UID label instead has no specified trusted label writer or enrollment contract in this read-only design.
findings.fix: Specify an implementable UID-to-placement/enrollment protocol in the shared owner, with exact API fields, trusted writer and allowed permissions, stale-object scheduling/GC ordering, and denial on Node deletion/recreation. If placement uses a name, make the separate admission/coverage mechanism check the actual immutable UID rather than claiming affinity does so. Preserve the no-node-write boundary unless an explicit justified change is made there. Add a pinned real-API same-name/new-UID schedule with old Deployment/ReplicaSet deletion delayed and a previously eligible permit; no old object may grant or establish new-node coverage.

findings.summary: Deployment surge can mint two global disruption credits for one observation.
findings.evidence: design.md:47-57 specifies replicas=1 Deployments and integer global minAvailable=N-1 for N registered ready deployments, but no rollout strategy or one-pod-per-UID enforcement. Kubernetes v1.36.5 defaults Deployments to RollingUpdate/maxSurge=25%, rounded up to one for replicas=1 (defaults.go:40-59; deployment_util.go:823-840). Its disruption controller counts every selected Ready pod and computes allowed=currentHealthy-desiredHealthy, without deduplicating node/Deployment identity (disruption.go:855-868,927-935). In a three-storage-node cluster A/B/C, let A/B share an RF2/minISR1 chunk and both have observed eligible permits. During C's ordinary rollout retain its old and new Ready slots before old-pod deletion; four Ready slot pods with minAvailable=2 create two credits. Concurrent A/B slot evictions both succeed, and their permit evictions can complete both unsafe drains. Re-reading observedGeneration does not make pod count equal distinct-node count. Primary sources: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/apis/apps/v1/defaults.go#L40-L59 ; https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/controller/deployment/util/deployment_util.go#L823-L840 ; https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L855-L868 ; https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.5/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L927-L935 .
findings.fix: Define the complete marker lifecycle/accounting invariant: at most one credit-bearing pod per admitted Node UID, stable expected-node accounting during outages, and creation/update/deletion ordering that cannot create extra credits or an uncovered drain. Pin an appropriate non-surging strategy or another concrete mechanism, and account for controller-driven pod deletion ignoring PDBs rather than treating strategy alone as proof. Add the three-node unrelated-rollout/concurrent-A-B-eviction fixture, lost-reply/restart cases and replacement/rollout coverage tests against the pinned API. Keep the final fail-closed choice with the shared owner.

findings.summary: The existing ListVolumes API can silently hide malformed metadata from the supposedly complete fail-closed pass.
findings.evidence: spec.md:35-38 requires malformed/missing metadata to deny; design.md:27-43 assumes complete enumeration and :122 explicitly leaves metadata RPC/service contracts unchanged. Actual meta/service/service.go:845-857 silently skips every header that json.Unmarshal cannot decode, returning successful IDs for the rest. Thus a stable damaged header for the only blocking volume is indistinguishable from no such volume, and no subsequent GetVolume is issued for it. Reviewed #77 design.md:16-39 fixes reads of named volumes and does not change ListVolumes enumeration. Client-side partial-error/oversize fixtures cannot detect a server-side silent omission.
findings.fix: Give the owner a concrete completeness contract for existing enumeration, minimally rejecting malformed published-header records with an explicit RPC error instead of skipping them, with required service/auth/client compatibility changes and file scope stated. Alternatively supply a specified read-only enumeration result that carries integrity/completeness failure. Do not bypass the metadata service or reopen #77. Add both-backend service-to-real-gRPC collector fixtures for a sole malformed header and mixed valid/malformed headers; both must revoke/deny permission rather than returning eligible/empty-cluster success.

findings.summary: The guard has no concrete composition with the now-canonical exact-store membership and paged-volume contracts.
findings.evidence: design.md:27-35 defines surviving distinct node IDs using alive and chunk ISR, with no schema/UUID/lifetime handling. Reviewed #90 contracts.md:12-28,42-49,83-87 replaces membership with exact (node,device_uuid) refs, projects current Node store UUID/generation and omits legacy node membership fields in ACTIVE mode; same node with a new store can be alive while the earned old UUID remains unavailable. Merely counting that node's alive flag would wrongly allow draining the remaining real copy; reading only legacy fields would instead hold all healthy identity-enabled clusters. #90 budgets.md:45-81 also supports legal paged_legacy volumes using ReadIdentityVolumePage with pinned incarnation/header/gate predicates. #69 design.md:24-31 currently permits Readers only four named methods, excluding that additive page RPC. #63 contains neither the adapter nor the whoever-lands-second auth/schema/page hook. #90 report HEAD read is c9231b243dceb196a0eccb615055887c9879bb73; its technical-clear snapshot is 331f337d3b847ff2d4faabc572f4ceae74837cd7. These remain proposed dependencies, not installed code.
findings.fix: Own an explicit last-to-land integration in the shared guard plan: validate supported schema and exact refs, count a surviving ref only when its earned UUID matches the observed live store, deduplicate by host/node, hold unknown/quarantined or pending-initial authority, and handle exact move endpoints. Define bounded ReadIdentityVolumePage accumulation with identical incarnation/header/gate predicates and no fallback to legacy node projections. Extend the reader's explicit method allowlist only for that read RPC when the adapter lands, preserving all mutation/replica refusals. Add healthy schema2, same-name/new-UUID, old-UUID return, same-node multiple-ref, pending-initial, paged-legacy, changed-page predicates and real-mTLS-reader allow/deny fixtures. Keep #69/#90 dependencies read-only; unsupported profiles must visibly hold.

findings.summary: The specified RBAC omits the resources used for Kubernetes status and Events.
findings.evidence: design.md:110-116 grants namespace access only to Deployments, pods, PDBs and Lease; :118-121 then requires owned ConfigMap status and rate-limited Events, as does spec.md:59-62. Neither configmaps nor core/events or events.k8s.io resources appear in the permission contract, and the S6 restriction to guard/controller/PDB/Lease objects does not include this status storage. The controller cannot publish the promised held reasons using the manifest rights as specified.
findings.fix: State the exact owned ConfigMap and Event API/verbs, namespace and resource-name constraints in S6/design/manifests; include only the permissions actually required for the chosen status representation. Add positive real-authorizer publication/update checks for the owned status object and event path alongside negative foreign-object, other-namespace, Secret, node and tenant-workload checks.

findings.summary: The acceptance procedure does not resolve its conflict with #83 refusing the lab VMs.
findings.evidence: intent.md What we want 7 and spec.md:69-73 require a real data-plane stop/return/drain/data verification on fl-a/fl-b; decisions.md:58-62 qualifies against that lab's k3s release. design.md:148-153 says only that #82/#83 constraints remain, without a runnable composed acceptance path. Reviewed #83 design.md:21-42 refuses detected virtual hardware before storage is opened/registered/listening and explicitly calls the existing lab VMs unqualified; no force/environment bypass exists. With #83 installed, fl-a cannot return with full ISR and the required data check cannot be set up on those VMs. Merely pinning Kubernetes v1.36.5 does not resolve data-plane admission.
findings.fix: Specify the conditional evidence matrix in the shared owner/wrapper: pre-#83 VM runs may be explicitly labeled exploratory observations of that historical stack; composed runtime acceptance requires qualified physical hosts running the pinned k3s/API release with dedicated RF2 data, while existing VMs must demonstrate expected admission refusal and cannot certify S8. Separate API-only eviction tests from the data-plane acceptance test and name prerequisites/skip-refusal outcomes without claiming either proves the other. Preserve explicit authorization and do not weaken #83.
